newsitem.title: DUBAI: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE WORRIED ABOUT RYDER TEAM STRENGTH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE WORRIED ABOUT RYDER TEAM STRENGTH.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie is worried Europe may not be able to field their strongest team for the defence of the Ryder Cup in September.
The European number one feels that with captain Seve Ballesteros having only two wild card picks, the 12-man squad to face the Americans at Valderrama, Spain, may lack vital experience.
The other places will go to the top 10 money winners after the BMW International on August 31.
Montgomerie fears that a player who competes in almost all the tour events could finish 15th each time and win enough money for a team spot.
"The Ryder Cup team should not be about good attendance. It should be about how you handle it mentally," he said on the eve of the Dubai Desert Classic starting on Thursday.
He wants an experienced team, not one with four or five newcomers which could happen under the present system.
"Three rookies is enough. In Ryder Cup week it's not how you can play golf. It's how you can handle yourself," he said.

He fears that if players such as Ian Woosnam or Bernhard Langer did not make the team by right, it could be difficult if Ballesteros felt compelled to select Nick Faldo, the hero of the 1995 triumph, and Swede Jesper Parnevik, who are both based on the U.S. Tour.
Parnevik is not a member of the European Tour and therefore his win in the Lancome Trophy qualifying event last October does not count towards selection.
This year he has had a string of top five finishes on the U.S. Tour and Ballesteros has conceded he is keeping a close eye on the Swede.
Ballesteros has urged ever since he was appointed captain last year that he would like to have four wild card picks, and Montgomerie has backed him.
But the Ryder Cup Committee - of which Ballesteros is not a member - ruled he will have only two because the team won in 1995 with that system.
"We won in spite of, not because of, having only two picks," Montgomerie said.
"I'd like the whole team to be picked," he added. "The top six or seven on the money list would undoubtedly be picked anyway but then the captain could select the rest."

He is worried that with only two picks, Ballesteros might have to choose from among four or five outstanding candidates, especially if Jose Maria Olazabal, making a comeback from injury this week, is playing well by then.
Montgomerie also called for a revival of the old Hennessy Cup event with golfers from Britain and Ireland facing those from Europe every second year between Ryder Cup events.
That would counter the advantage he felt the Americans have gained from the new President's Cup, where they face golfers from the rest of the world except Europe in the years between the Ryder Cup.
"That's like a trial run for the Ryder Cup for them," he said.
